title: Estimate before you build
objective: Use rough multiplication and units to judge how big a system must be before designing it.

sources.title: Bentley, Programming Pearls, 2nd ed. (Addison-Wesley, 2000): column 7, "The Back of the Envelope"

simplifies: Every number here is illustrative, not measured. Real estimates also count copies (backups, replicas), growth over time and overheads, and use your own system's figures.

options.explanation: Right, in decimal units: 1,000 KB = 1 MB, and 1,000 MB = 1 GB.

quiz.prompt: Your estimate says 25,000 GB. What does that tell you before writing any code?

options.explanation: 25,000 GB is 25 TB: more than one ordinary disk.

options.text: Plan for several disks or a storage service, plus extra copies for safety
options.explanation: Right. The order of magnitude (terabytes) changes the design, which is exactly why you estimate first.
Maybe the inputs are off, but a big number is a reason to check them, not to dismiss the result.
